title: Conditional protection for third-party online content
current_status: In force in the official current text reviewed
source_currency: Official U.S. Code current through Public Law 119-142 (2026-11-10), opened during this review.
effective_date: Historical commencement date not independently re-established; operative status checked against the official current compilation.
summary: Section 230 limits specified publisher/speaker liability for information supplied by another information-content provider. The statutory definitions and exceptions govern whether a service and claim qualify. A routing service displaying third-party user content may raise this framework, but the section does not establish blanket immunity for the provider’s own route creation or development.
scope: Qualifying interactive computer services and users, third-party information, and claims satisfying the statute’s conditions; applicability is function- and claim-specific.
classification_rationale: This generally applicable online-liability law lies outside the AB 2015 road-intervention scope. It may govern qualifying legal action against a routing provider, but does not expressly name routing apps or impose a route-choice rule.
operative_evidence: No provider or user of an interactive computer service shall be treated as the publisher or speaker
penalties_and_liability: The reviewed provision supplies conditional liability protections rather than a fixed monetary penalty; subsection (e) preserves specified categories of law.
exceptions: Federal criminal law, intellectual property, communications privacy, specified trafficking claims, and provider-created/developed information require separate treatment.
notes: A valid general-law classification does not establish immunity for a particular app, algorithm, statement or lawsuit.

summary: The section establishes a fourteen-foot vehicle-height limit with specified exceptions. Owners and operators remain responsible for determining sufficient vertical clearance. scope: Washington vehicle owners/operators, responsible highway authorities and owners of overhead structures.
classification_rationale: Clearance and vehicle-height rules constrain safe commercial-route eligibility through operators and authorities rather than app-specific duties.

exceptions: Authorized emergency vehicles and reasonably necessary public-utility repair equipment; liability qualifications depend on height and proper signs.
